Quantī cōnstat?

phrase: the genitive of price, quantī

how much does it cost?

The price asked about is in the genitive, quantī, with cōnstat, emis, vēndis; so are tantī, plūris, minōris. A price named is in the ablative: magnō, parvō, asse (see cost a lot).

Examples

  • Tum pater eam interrogāvit: «Quantī cōnstant?» Pretiō audītō nummōs dēnumerāvit, vēnditrīx nummulōs reddidit.

    Then Dad asked her, “How much are they?” When he heard the price he counted out the money, and the stallholder gave back the change.Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • dīc quotus et quantī cupiās cēnāre

    tell me how many of you there will be, and at what price you want to dineMart. 14.218.1

  • ego … paenitēre tantī nōn emō

    I don’t buy regret at that priceGell. 1.8.6

  • Quantī haec cōnstant?

    How much do these cost?Traupman 113

  • Centum dēnāriīs cōnstat.

    It costs 100 denarii.Traupman 297

See also price, cost a lot, pay, change.
